Visual identity guidelines

Count the crossing, never the person.

Contar el cruce, nunca a la persona.

Version 1.0 · October 2026
Andean Transit Migration Data Hub (ATMDH / OAMT)
Departmental Youth Council of Santa Cruz, Bolivia · Asociación Juvenil Bookcubers

1 · The ideaOne crossing, twelve cells, and a protected one

The Hub counts people who cross the central Andean corridor between Peru and Bolivia, and it is built so that nobody can be followed. The symbol says both things at once. It is a stepped diamond, the form that recurs in Andean textiles, and it echoes the chakana, the stepped cross whose name is usually translated as bridge.

  • Lago, left of the axis. The Peruvian side of the corridor.
  • Noche, the axis and the right side. The Bolivian side, and the corridor that runs through both.
  • The ochre ring. Desaguadero: one bridge, two municipalities, the only point where the corridor is literally a single place.
  • The hollow cell. A protected cell, one with fewer than ten people. It is drawn so the reader can see that it exists and cannot be shown. It is never drawn as zero and never left out.
  • Twelve cells. One for each node of the Hub, around a center that stays open.
The name of the symbol is “El Cruce”, the crossing.It is the unit the Hub counts. The person who crosses is never the unit.

How the name is written

ATMDH / OAMT is the full signature: ATMDH in English (Andean Transit Migration Data Hub) and OAMT in Spanish. In running text use “the Hub”, “el Hub” or “ATMDH”. Spanish descriptor: Hub de Datos de Migración de Tránsito Andina.

Signature line

Count the crossing, never the person. / Contar el cruce, nunca a la persona. It is optional. Use it on covers, social cards and presentation closings, not next to the logo in small spaces.

3 · Clear space and minimum sizeGive the symbol room to breathe

Clear space

Keep one cell of the symbol free on every side, about 17% of its width. For the lockups, measure that cell from the symbol and apply it to the whole block. Nothing enters the shaded area: no text, no edge of the page, no other logo.

Backgrounds

Full color on Hielo or white. Reversed on Noche. One-color light on Lago or other dark brand colors. Never on a busy photograph or a saturated gradient: put a Noche panel under it.

5 · TypographyOne family, two weights, tabular numbers

ATMDH
Bahnschrift SemiBold. Wordmark, titles, section labels. Wordmark tracking +7%.
Recorded events by municipality and month
Bahnschrift Regular. Subtitles, body text, interface.
3.1401.354.44185.000n<10
Numbers use tabular figures so columns line up. The suppression marker is always written n<10.

Fallback

Bahnschrift ships with Windows 10 and 11. Where it is missing, use Segoe UI, then the system sans-serif. The logo files already carry the wordmark as outlines, so they never depend on the font. The website uses the system font stack on purpose, so that it loads offline with no remote fonts.

Writing

  • Say “recorded events”, never “population” or “number of migrants”.
  • Say “people who cross” or “people in transit”. Avoid “flows” as a subject without people behind it, and avoid “illegal”.
  • Write every public text in English and Spanish. Spanish first on Bolivian and Peruvian channels, English first on international ones.
  • Dates as 2026-10-27 in data, “27 October 2026” in prose. Keep sentences short and put the number first.
ATMDH / OAMT · Visual identity v1.0 · October 20266

6 · Visual rules that protect peopleThe identity follows the privacy design

These rules are not taste. They are the same promises the system makes in code, applied to every poster, slide and post.

1. Never show an identifiable migrant.No faces, no documents, no children, no license plates, no photographs taken at a crossing without written consent and a reason that belongs to the story. When in doubt, show the place or the object (a bridge, a bus terminal, a shelter door), not the person.
2. Never plot a person.No map with one dot per individual and no route drawn for one traveler. Maps show nodes and totals by municipality and month, nothing finer.
3. A protected cell is hollow, never zero.If a figure is below ten, draw the hollow cell or the hatched bar and write n<10. Do not print 0 and do not hide the row.
4. Say what the number is.Every count carries the label “recorded events” and its source. Every forecast carries its band. A line without a band is not published.
5. Credit the sources.The Hub reuses figures from INE Bolivia, INEI, Migraciones, DIGEMIG, UNHCR, IOM, Chile’s PDI. Name them next to the figure, as the site does.
6. Be honest about the stage.When a figure comes from a demonstration or an estimate, label it as such on the same slide.

Photography

Landscape and infrastructure at altitude: the Desaguadero bridge, the El Alto skyline, Lake Titicaca, the Pisiga road. Natural light, no filters, no saturated color grading. Place text on a Noche panel, never directly on the picture.

ATMDH / OAMT · Visual identity v1.0 · October 20267

7 · What not to doEight ways to break the symbol

Do not stretchDo not rotateDo not recolorNo shadows or glow
Do not fade itNot on busy backgroundsDo not squash itDo not flatten the colors

Never

  • Fill the hollow cell, or remove the ring. They carry the meaning.
  • Add cells, or arrange the twelve cells in a different shape.
  • Retype ATMDH in another typeface, change its tracking, or separate it from the symbol in the lockups.
  • Place the logo inside a circle or a badge of another organization’s color.

Partners

Next to the logos of other organizations, keep the ATMDH logo at the same optical height and respect its clear space. Do not imply endorsement: use the line “Developed in the Departmental Youth Council of Santa Cruz” only if the Council has agreed.

Using this identity in a co-branded post

  1. Photo of the speaker or place on the left, text on a Noche panel on the right.
  2. Horizontal logo, reversed, bottom left, with the clear space respected.
  3. One ochre element only: the ring in the logo, or a single highlighted figure.
  4. Caption in two languages, with the sources named.
